text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Wednesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Government factions in parliament support the candidature of Vassily Melnik as finance minister. They still have doubts about Melnik being in violation of the law on the prevention of corruption. Some suggested Shkele was quick to support Melnik because Saimnieks, the biggest parliamentary party, had threatened it would otherwise withdraw from the coalition.
- Riga council has applied for exclusive broadcasting rights on TV Channel Seven, closed at the end of 1996.
- A 10,000 lats reward has been offered by the prosecutor's office to anyone helping the investigation into the robbery of a post office van last week.
- An 11-year boy whose palm was torn off by a ski-lift last Sunday has undergone successful microsurgery.
- Riga Commercial Bank became the first Latvian bank to be given a credit rating by Thomson BankWatch. The agency gave the bank a long-term rating of BB- and a short-term one of LC-2.

- The cabinet approved regulations on income declarations of both residents and non-residents. The number of those asked to declare their income will drop to 150,000 to 200,000 from one million in 1996 as it will now mostly comprise entrepreneurs.
- British Airways wants to fly to Riga.
- The ending of export tariffs may lead to the bankruptcy of 750 timber companies, a timber industry leader says.
